Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Creative Group Facilitator, Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Team,
I recently came across your Creative Group Facilitator opening and wanted to introduce myself. I understand the position may have been filled, but I would welcome consideration for this or future opportunities with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

My background brings together adolescent behavioral health support, recovery group facilitation, visual arts education, and fitness and wellness programming. 

At Family Center for Recovery, I supported adolescents and adults in structured treatment settings. At Futures Recovery Healthcare, I facilitated recovery support groups and helped alumni connect with resources and coping strategies. More recently, as an art teacher, I have designed creative activities that encourage confidence, expression, and engagement.

I am especially drawn to opportunities to help young people strengthen self-esteem and positive self-talk through art, movement, drama-inspired expression, and mindfulness. My approach values practical DBT-informed skills and creative activities as complements to the work of licensed treatment professionals.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my experience might support your programming. I have attached my resume for your consideration. 

Thank you for your time.

Warm regards, Jennifer Winston

Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT
Kings Mountain, NC
(704) 418-2440 | celditz@gmail.com

October 26, 2026

Hiring Committee
Launch AWA NC
Re: Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Clinic Director – Adolescent Mental Health position with Launch AWA NC. As a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist with more than 25 years of experience in clinical and child-and-family services, including over 15 years in program and clinical leadership, I bring a combination of clinical expertise, operational management, staff development, and a strong commitment to improving outcomes for children, adolescents, and families. I am excited about the opportunity to apply my experience to a role focused on adolescent mental health and the delivery of high-quality, accessible clinical services.

In my current role as Director of Programs at Children’s Homes of Cleveland County/Core Family Services, I provide senior clinical and operational leadership across outpatient therapy, residential, independent living, and adoption programs. I also serve as Clinical Director of outpatient therapy, where I oversee clinical quality, clinician recruitment and supervision, service capacity, reimbursement, compliance, and ongoing program development. Throughout my tenure, I have worked to strengthen clinical services, support staff effectiveness, and ensure that programs meet the needs of the individuals and families they serve while maintaining appropriate clinical, contractual, and regulatory standards.

My experience has provided me with a strong understanding of the balance required to lead a successful behavioral health clinic. I have experience developing clinical capacity in response to community needs, supporting clinicians through supervision and consultation, managing after-hours clinical coverage for therapeutic emergencies, and collaborating with executive leadership on staffing, budgeting, and organizational planning. I believe effective clinical leadership requires both a commitment to sound clinical practice and the ability to build the systems, relationships, and processes that allow clinicians to provide meaningful, consistent care.

I also bring extensive experience in trauma-informed care, quality improvement, and clinical standards. As a Statewide Clinical Coach with Benchmarks NC Partnering for Excellence, I train, review, and evaluate trauma-intensive clinical assessments completed by clinicians across North Carolina, providing feedback and supporting consistency with established clinical standards. Additionally, I coordinate my agency’s performance and quality improvement and accreditation activities, including staff training, record reviews, corrective action planning, and continuous improvement initiatives. These experiences have strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical practices, identify opportunities for improvement, support professional development, and promote accountability while maintaining a focus on quality care.

In addition to my clinical background, I hold a Master of Science in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Master of Business Administration. This combination allows me to approach clinical leadership with an understanding of both the therapeutic needs of adolescents and families and the operational and financial considerations necessary to sustain and grow effective services. I value collaborative leadership, clear communication, thoughtful decision-making, and creating an environment where clinicians feel supported in their work and equipped to provide the highest quality of care.

Throughout my career, I have remained committed to serving children and families, particularly those impacted by trauma and other significant life challenges. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my experience to Launch AWA NC and help strengthen mental health services for adolescents. Given my extensive experience, clinical background, and leadership responsibilities, I would also welcome a conversation about compensation. I recognize that the position has a posted salary range; however, I am seeking compensation above that range that more fully reflects my qualifications and the value I would bring to the role. I hope there may be flexibility to discuss a package that aligns with my experience and the position’s responsibilities.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical background, leadership experience, and commitment to serving adolescents and families could contribute to the continued success of Launch AWA NC.

Sincerely,
Celena Ditz, MS, LMFT

candidates.cover_letter:
TY MATTHEWS, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)
Rock Hill, SC • (704) 999-3605 • Matthewstydsw27@gmail.com

October 27, 2026
Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Mooresville, NC

Re: Clinic Director: Adolescent Mental Health | Launch AWA North Carolina

Dear Hiring Committee:
I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position leading the launch of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s first North Carolina clinic. As a licensed clinical social work and case management leader with more than 15 years of experience across behavioral health, healthcare, higher education, and community services, I offer the clinical supervision, operational leadership, and change-management experience needed to build a strong program from the ground up. AWA’s opportunity to create a focused, family-centered PHP/IOP clinic for adolescents is especially compelling to me because it combines direct clinical impact with the chance to shape culture, quality, and sustainable growth from day one.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. These experiences would enable me to recruit and develop clinicians, establish clear clinical and documentation standards, guide level-of-care decisions, and build trusted relationships with families and referral partners across North Carolina.

I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. My Master of Social Work and ongoing Doctor of Social Work studies in leadership further support my ability to connect evidence-informed clinical practice with disciplined operations and organizational growth.

AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.
Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Program Coordinator position. What drew me to this opportunity is the chance to support adolescents and their families during a time when having consistent, compassionate, and accessible mental health care can make such a meaningful difference.

Throughout my experience in behavioral health, I have found that the work I value most involves supporting children and families while contributing to the teams responsible for their care. As an RBT and Student Analyst, I have worked closely with children and families, assisted with initial assessments and reassessments, contributed to treatment planning, supported parent training, and collaborated with multidisciplinary providers. These experiences have given me a strong understanding of the importance of communication, documentation, and teamwork in behavioral health services.

In addition to my clinical experience, my previous role as a Health Assistant gave me a strong foundation in healthcare administration and remote client support. I worked with clients to verify insurance benefits, reviewed coverage information, assisted with claims and payment-related inquiries, and handled a high volume of calls while communicating with English- and Spanish-speaking families. My experience as a Child Protective Investigator also shaped the way I approach family communication. It taught me the importance of listening without judgment, handling sensitive situations with care, and recognizing when concerns need to be communicated or escalated. I believe these skills would be especially valuable when supporting adolescents and families participating in AWA's virtual program.

As a bilingual English and Spanish speaker, I would love the opportunity to help families feel comfortable navigating the admissions process, staying connected with the program, and understanding important updates. I am particularly interested in bringing together my behavioral health and administrative experience in a role that allows me to contribute to the day-to-day operations of a program making a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, experience, and genuine interest in supporting young people could contribute to the AWA team.

Warmly,
Josmari Arroyo

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Utilization Review Specialist position. I have over 13 years of experience in healthcare, and in my current role with United Billing, I have gained valuable experience in behavioral health utilization review.

My responsibilities include handling initial authorizations, pre-certifications, and concurrent reviews, as well as monitoring authorized units and coverage dates. I would appreciate the opportunity to bring my experience and skills to your team. Thank you for considering my application, and I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Irene Dupera

These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining your team at the Adolescent Wellness Center. I am currently pursuing my bachelor's degree in Human Services with a concentration in Substance Abuse, and I would love the opportunity to work in an environment where I can help young people navigate challenges and make positive changes in their lives.

I have a genuine passion for helping others, especially those who may be struggling with mental health, substance use, difficult home situations, or simply trying to find their place in the world. I believe young people need someone who will listen without judgment, treat them with respect, and remind them that their current circumstances do not have to determine their future.

I have completed 46 hours of Peer Recovery Support Specialist training, including ethics, where I gained knowledge about communication, confidentiality, professional boundaries, and providing support to individuals facing difficult situations. I believe this training, along with my education and personal life experiences, would allow me to bring compassion, patience, and understanding to your team.

One thing I feel strongly about is that young people deserve to feel heard and supported rather than judged or overlooked. Sometimes having just one person who believes in them can make a difference. I would be grateful for the opportunity to be part of an organization that helps adolescents build confidence, develop healthy coping skills, and work toward a better future.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my dedication, education, and willingness to learn could contribute to your team and the young people you serve.

Sincerely,

Heather Rodeheaver

Managing multiple responsibilities has strengthened my organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to balance competing priorities while providing consistent, compassionate support.

One of the aspects of my work that I value most is building trusting relationships and creating an environment where individuals feel welcomed, heard, and supported. I believe that a safe, encouraging, and nonjudgmental environment helps people feel comfortable engaging with others, working through challenges, and building confidence in their abilities. I take pride in my strong client satisfaction ratings and in creating positive experiences through thoughtful communication, consistency, and reliable follow-through.


Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and commitment to supporting others align with your team’s needs.

Sincerely,

Jennifer Misko

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am pleased to submit my application for the Virtual Admission Coordinator position within your organization. I hold a Master of Social Work (MSW) from Ana G. Méndez University and am a Certified Behavioral Health Case Manager Supervisor (CBHCMS). My professional background combines extensive experience in behavioral health services, patient assessments, care coordination, case management, administrative operations, and client-centered communication.

Throughout my career, I have worked closely with individuals and families seeking mental health, substance abuse treatment, and community-based services. My responsibilities have included conducting initial assessments, reviewing eligibility and service needs, coordinating referrals, facilitating admissions, maintaining confidential records, and ensuring effective communication between clients, healthcare providers, and multidisciplinary teams.

Through my professional experience with UC Behavioral Health & Social Services and Golden Phoenix Mental Health, I have developed strong organizational and administrative skills, including managing patient documentation, coordinating services, monitoring referrals, supporting intake procedures, and maintaining compliance with HIPAA, Medicaid requirements, and organizational policies.

I am particularly interested in this position because it allows me to combine my clinical knowledge with my administrative and interpersonal skills to support an efficient, compassionate, and well-organized admission process. I understand the importance of providing a positive first experience for patients and families while ensuring accurate documentation, timely follow-up, and effective coordination of services.

Additionally, I am bilingual in English and Spanish, proficient in electronic health records, digital documentation, virtual communication platforms, and Microsoft Office applications. I am comfortable working independently in a remote environment while maintaining productivity, confidentiality, professionalism, and effective collaboration with team members.

I believe my background in behavioral health, patient services, admissions coordination, and administrative leadership would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your organization.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my professional experience, qualifications, and dedication to quality patient services align with the needs of your team.

I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,

Ingrid Cruz, MSW, CBHCMS.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a professional background in behavioral health, care coordination, substance use counseling, and healthcare administration, I am confident in my ability to provide compassionate, organized, and effective support to individuals and families seeking treatment.

In my current role as a Care Coordinator and Substance Use Counselor at Intermountain Centers, I work closely with adolescents, families, healthcare providers, and community agencies to coordinate behavioral health services and ensure individuals receive appropriate levels of care. My responsibilities include conducting assessments, coordinating referrals, facilitating Child and Family Team (CFT) meetings, assisting families with treatment planning, and supporting individuals through complex behavioral health challenges. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate with individuals in distress, identify service needs, and guide families through the treatment process with empathy and professionalism.

I also bring experience working within Arizona’s behavioral health system, including coordinating services with Medicaid-funded programs, maintaining accurate clinical documentation, and collaborating with multidisciplinary treatment teams. I understand the importance of timely follow-up, confidentiality, HIPAA compliance, and clear communication when helping individuals access mental health and substance use treatment.

As a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking professional, I am able to support diverse populations and help reduce language barriers that may prevent individuals and families from accessing care. I hold a Master of Business Administration (MBA) and a Master of Healthcare Administration (MHA), and I am currently completing my Master’s degree in Addiction Psychology at Arizona State University. This combination of clinical knowledge and administrative education allows me to approach admissions coordination with both compassion and operational efficiency.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to serve as a supportive first point of contact for adolescents, adults, and families during challenging moments. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be overwhelming, and I believe every individual deserves to be met with patience, dignity, and reassurance.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, dedication, and commitment to accessible behavioral healthcare to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications align with the needs of your programs.

Sincerely, 
Leslie Bright

RE: Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 20 years of experience in behavioral health, residential services, and program operations, I bring a strong background in leadership, staff development, clinical coordination, and quality improvement. I am excited about the opportunity to contribute my experience to a growing program focused on improving access to mental health services for adolescents and their families.

Throughout my career, I have held progressively responsible positions, including Behavioral Health Program Manager and Coordinator, overseeing daily operations across multiple outpatient services. In these roles, I supervised more than 21 employees, coordinated multidisciplinary teams, monitored program productivity and spending, and supported operational improvements to strengthen service delivery. My experience also includes admissions coordination, community referrals, staff scheduling, documentation oversight, and maintaining compliance with Medicaid, DCF, CARF, and HIPAA requirements.

My professional background has allowed me to develop a strong understanding of the importance of balancing clinical quality with operational efficiency. I recognize that building a successful program requires more than providing services. It involves developing strong referral relationships, supporting staff, monitoring performance, identifying opportunities for growth, and ensuring that individuals and families receive timely, coordinated care.

Although much of my recent clinical and operational experience has focused on adults with mental health and co-occurring substance use disorders, my earlier experience providing behavioral support services has strengthened my understanding of individualized care, family collaboration, and the importance of early intervention. I believe these experiences provide a valuable foundation for supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy's family-centered approach to adolescent treatment.

I have completed all requirements for my Master of Social Work degree through Walden University and am awaiting official degree conferral. I also hold the Certified Behavioral Health Case Manager Supervisor (CBHCMS) credential and have submitted my application for Florida Registered Clinical Social Work Intern registration. These professional milestones reflect my continued commitment to clinical development, ethical practice, and effective behavioral health leadership.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my leadership experience, operational knowledge, and commitment to quality care to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to the continued development of its Virtual IOP through strong team leadership, community partnerships, and a consistent focus on program performance and client outcomes.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and professional goals align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Michelle Antonia Rivera
CBHCMS
MSW Program Completed

questionnaire.response: My supervisor would likely say my biggest area for growth was delegation. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my enthusiastic interest in the Operations Manager role. With over a decade of operations leadership, regulatory compliance, and team development experience, paired with my upcoming Bachelor of Science in Behavioral and Social Sciences from North Carolina Central University, I am uniquely positioned to bridge operational rigor with compassionate, client-centered program delivery. After building a successful career leading high-compliance operations in the financial sector, I am intentionally transitioning my career path to align my operational expertise with my academic foundation in behavioral studies—supporting structured, safe, and effective environments for clients and clinical teams alike.   

While my recent leadership tenure was in financial services, the core pillars of my work directly mirror the demands of PHP/IOP and behavioral health operations:

Program Operations, Scheduling & Workflow Optimization: As Back Office Operations Manager at Varo Bank, I oversaw daily multi-functional workflows, streamlined case intake and documentation procedures to improve accuracy and turnaround times, and implemented KPI/KRI frameworks to drive operational consistency. Certified as a Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, I excel at balancing census/workload distribution, managing shifting priorities, and optimizing administrative and facility processes.   

Team Leadership & Accountability: I bring extensive supervisory experience hiring, coaching, and mentoring staff through Individual Development Plans (IDPs), performance evaluations, and skill-based training to foster accountability and internal growth. My earlier background as a GED Lab Facilitator at Central Piedmont Community College and Case Manager/Employment Specialist at ResCare WorkForce Services further grounds my ability to guide, support, and empower diverse individuals in structured learning and service settings.   

Compliance, Documentation & Risk Management: Having operated in heavily regulated environments governed by federal standards (FDIC, BSA, GLBA, REG E/Z), I maintain uncompromising attention to documentation integrity, recurring system audits, incident investigation, and regulatory adherence—skills that translate seamlessly to healthcare compliance, incident reporting, and safety standards.   

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Escalation Resolution: Throughout my career, I have partnered closely with cross-functional stakeholders—including risk, legal, compliance, external agencies, and leadership—while serving as a calm, decisive point of contact for complex escalations. In a behavioral health setting, I am eager to partner with clinical leadership, therapists, admissions, and families to maintain a cohesive, supportive environment that aids in de-escalation and positive client outcomes.   

My transition into behavioral health operations represents the deliberate convergence of my professional strengths and my academic focus on human behavior and social systems. I am confident in my ability to step into a fast-paced clinical operations environment, bring structure and stability to daily program logistics, and support your staff so they can focus on delivering exceptional care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my operations leadership and behavioral science background can support your program's mission and team.

Sincerely,
Taylor Pittman

questionnaire.text: If we asked this supervisor about your performance, what would they say was your most significant area for growth, and why?
questionnaire.response: If my supervisor were asked about my most significant area for growth, they would point to my ambition in scaling our team’s leadership development beyond daily metrics—specifically by tailoring individual professional growth plans to align with each team member's distinct career goals, fostering deeper cross-functional engagement and team-building initiatives, and scaling our onboarding and training framework to seamlessly integrate offshore analysts.  While I have a strong track record of driving operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and day-to-day workflow execution, my supervisor and I recognized that as our operations grew, my leadership impact needed to intentionally expand into these broader strategic pillars. Why we focused here: In fast-paced, high-compliance environments, it is easy to become hyper-focused on immediate case turnaround times, KPIs, and risk mitigation. However, to build long-term organizational resilience and a sustainable culture of accountability, I needed to lean further into customized mentorship.   How I’ve grown: I leaned into this challenge by implementing structured coaching models—such as Individual Development Plans (IDPs)—and dedicating intentional bandwidth to designing rigorous, structured onboarding pathways and training materials for our offshore partners. This not only closed knowledge gaps and accelerated ramp-up times, but it also empowered local and remote analysts alike to see a clear path for internal growth, ultimately elevating our overall team performance and engagement.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Admissions Counselor position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With six years of experience in education as a Teacher's Assistant and Guidance Counselor, along with over five years of experience in healthcare, including mental health and substance use services, I bring a diverse professional background and a genuine passion for helping adolescents and families navigate life's challenges.

Throughout my career, I have developed a strong ability to build meaningful connections with individuals from all walks of life. My experience has taught me that effective guidance begins with understanding, compassion, and the ability to meet people where they are without judgment. Whether working with students, patients, or families, I believe every individual deserves to feel respected, heard, and valued. I approach every interaction with the understanding that I am not above the person seeking support; I am there to walk alongside them, offer guidance, and help them recognize their own potential.

My background in mental health and substance use services has further strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, navigate sensitive situations, and establish trust with individuals experiencing vulnerable moments in their lives. My own personal experiences with loss and adversity have also shaped my perspective, deepening my appreciation for resilience, compassion, and the importance of having someone who genuinely believes in you. These experiences have reinforced my commitment to treating every individual with dignity rather than defining them by their circumstances.

My colleagues would describe me as ambitious, focused, reliable, and grounding. I take pride in my ability to bridge the gap between professionalism and relatability, creating connections that allow people to feel comfortable, supported, and understood. I believe my combined experience in education, healthcare, mental health, and substance use services gives me a unique perspective that aligns with the mission of supporting adolescents and their families through important and sometimes difficult transitions.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because I value the opportunity to be part of an organization that prioritizes adolescent wellness, personal growth, and individualized support. I would be honored to bring my professional experience, personal perspective, and genuine dedication to helping others to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, compassion, and commitment to serving others would make me a valuable addition to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Amanda Nieves-Rodriguez

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Program Coordinator – Bilingual, Adolescent Mental Health position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With professional experience in nonprofit case management, a background supporting vulnerable individuals and families, fluency in Spanish, and my ongoing pursuit of a Master of Social Work degree at Simmons University, I believe I bring a combination of skills and passion that aligns well with this opportunity.
Throughout my experience working with refugee and newcomer populations, I have developed strong skills in case coordination, client advocacy, resource navigation, and building meaningful relationships with individuals from diverse backgrounds. My work has required effective communication, organization, adaptability, and the ability to navigate sensitive situations with empathy and professionalism. I understand the importance of creating supportive environments where individuals feel heard, respected, and empowered.
I am particularly interested in this position because of its focus on adolescent mental health. I strongly believe that young people deserve access to compassionate, culturally responsive support, especially during important developmental stages of their lives. I am passionate about helping adolescents and families navigate challenges, access appropriate resources, and feel supported throughout their journeys. As a bilingual Spanish speaker, I would also be excited to help reduce language barriers and improve accessibility for Spanish-speaking families.
My graduate studies in social work have further strengthened my interest in mental health, advocacy, social justice, and supporting underserved populations. I am eager to apply my professional experience while continuing to grow in the behavioral health field. I also bring the ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, communicate effectively in virtual environments, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams.
I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my experience, bilingual communication skills, organizational abilities, and dedication to supporting adolescents and families to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how I could contribute to your team.
Sincerely,
Giselle Santos
